text: dsh-model-advanced 是 DeepSeek Harness 的 Web 插件，在 Models 设置页增加逐模型高级设置，并在主机侧调整模型请求。它可为每个 provider/model 配置默认推理等级，让未指定等级的会话沿用该值；还可为不能看图的模型指定图像委托模型，将图像转成文字说明留在会话中，并提供 inspect_image 供追问。适合需要按模型管理推理方式或让文本模型处理图像的 Harness 用户。图像会交给所配置的模型处理；无需在插件中填写额外密钥。

dsh-model-advanced adds per-model reasoning defaults and image delegation to DeepSeek Harness. Set defaults in the Models card; requests without an effort use the saved value. A configured vision model can describe images for a text-only model, with follow-up questions through inspect_image.
想让不同模型分别使用各自的默认推理等级。
文本模型收到图片时，能否让另一个视觉模型先读图并把结果留在对话里？
Let me ask follow-up questions about an image through a model that can read it.
dsh-model-advanced 的功能「逐模型推理默认值」：在 Models 设置页为每个模型选择默认 reasoning effort；模型切换或请求未指定等级时，插件将该配置用于请求。
dsh-model-advanced 的功能「图像委托与追问」：为文本模型配置图像委托后，带图请求会调用委托模型并将文字转录附入会话；之后可用 inspect_image 及图像 id 提问。
dsh-model-advanced 使用前须知：启用图像委托后，图像附件会随模型调用发送给所配置的图像委托模型；实际服务由该模型的 Harness 路由决定。

dsh-model-advanced README · dsh-model-advanced：Per-model default reasoning level and image handoff for text-only models — added to
the existing **Settings → Models** page.

Model adapters describe a model once, provider-wide and statically. Two things an
agent actually needs cannot be expressed that way:

dsh-model-advanced README · dsh-model-advanced：- **The level a conversation should start at, per model.** A fast model and a
  reasoning model on the same provider usually want different defaults, but an adapter
  exposes a single provider-wide effort.
- **What happens when a text-only model is handed an image.** Today the image is
  dropped or the turn fails. It should be read by a model that *can* see, and the
  reading should stay in the conversation.

dsh-model-advanced README · dsh-model-advanced：This plugin adds a card at the bottom of the Models page that configures both, and
implements the runtime behaviour behind them.

*The card this plugin adds, at the bottom of **Settings → Models**: a starting reasoning
level for each model, and — for a model that cannot see — the model that reads images on
its behalf.*

dsh-model-advanced README · Install：Requires a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) install
with the plugin manager.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:drm-nz/dsh-model-advanced
```

Then **restart the app**. This plugin has a host half (`lib/index.js`) and a browser
half (`lib/client.js`); the host half loads at boot, and the browser half is served
from the installed package, so neither picks up without a restart.

dsh-model-advanced README · From a local checkout：```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-model-advanced
```

or add the `link:` dependency to the profile's `package.json`, run `pnpm install` there,
and restart. A linked package resolves its dependencies and peers from its own
directory, so they must be installed there too.

dsh-model-advanced README · From a local checkout：The shipped `cordis.patch.yml` names its entry **bare** (`dsh-model-advanced`), not
relatively. A `link:` install's real directory sits outside `node_modules`, and this
plugin imports Harness packages, so a bare name resolves through the profile's
dependency mapping — a relative name would bypass it and the import would fail.

To remove it:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-model-advanced
```

dsh-model-advanced README · From a local checkout：Requires the Harness packages it builds on (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`,
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`) to resolve from the profile, and
they should match the running Harness version — the plugin decorates runtime
prototypes, so it is version-coupled by nature. See *Compatibility* below.

dsh-model-advanced README · The card：One row per configured model, under the model list:

| Column | What it sets |
|---|---|
| Model | The model's name, provider, and id |
| **Default reasoning level** | The level a conversation starts at when it has not picked one. Empty option = no override |
| **Image understanding** | For a model that cannot read images: the configured model that reads them on its behalf |

dsh-model-advanced README · The card：Both choices are stored in this plugin's own settings namespace (`model-advanced`),
keyed `provider/model` — not in the adapters'. That is what keeps two models on one
provider independent, and what lets a model the adapters cannot describe still get a
default.
dsh-model-advanced README · How the default reasoning level is applied：Four seams, because a level can be chosen — or never chosen — in several places:
section: How the default reasoning level is applied

text:
dsh-model-advanced README · How the default reasoning level is applied：1. **`resolveModelInfo`** is decorated so the model catalogue *states* the configured
   level, and so the composer's Effort menu opens on it.
2. **`resolveCallConfig`** is decorated so selecting a model *without* naming a level
   saves the configured level instead of the adapter's own default.
3. An **`agent/request` waterfall** covers entry points that never pick a level at all.
4. A **startup reconciliation** (once, after the composition transaction settles)
   aligns the global default selection with the configured level.
section: How the default reasoning level is applied

text: dsh-model-advanced README · How the default reasoning level is applied：Both prototype decorations are restored on dispose.
section: How the default reasoning level is applied

text:
dsh-model-advanced README · How image handoff works：Configure a delegate for a model that does not read images. Then, when a turn carries
an image:

dsh-model-advanced README · How image handoff works：1. The delegate is called **once**, with a layout-preserving transcription
   instruction: a one-line summary, reading order, every text region with its
   approximate bounding box on a 0–1000 scale, tables as GFM, and notes for diagrams
   and UI state.
2. The result is appended to the step as an image transcript note naming the image id.
3. That note carries a `[dsh-image-handoff:<id>]` marker which is read back from
   session history, so retries and later turns **never re-bill the delegate**.
4. The image itself stays in the conversation; the wire to the text-only model still
   carries a placeholder, never the image. The transcript is what the model reads.

dsh-model-advanced README · How image handoff works：For follow-up questions the model calls:

```text
inspect_image(image_id, question)
```

which hands the same image to the delegate again with the question. This exists so a
text-only model is not stuck with a single fixed reading of an image forever.

A delegate failure does not end the turn — it becomes a note in the transcript saying
what could not be read.

dsh-model-advanced README · Discovering which models read images：Capability is resolved in this order, cheapest first:

1. **The provider's own configuration** — the model's declared input modalities in
   its settings namespace.
2. **`discoverModels`**, asked only for models the configuration does not describe, so
   an ordinary page load stays offline.
3. **Inference from the same model id** served by another configured route.
4. **A checkbox** — *"This model reads images"* — when all of the above are unknown,
   which pins the answer for that model.

dsh-model-advanced README · Configure by hand：The card writes this namespace; it can also be edited directly.

```yaml
- id: model-advanced
  config:
    modelDefaults:
      "deepseek/deepseek-chat": high

dsh-model-advanced README · Configure by hand：| Key | Shape | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `modelDefaults` | `provider/model` → effort id | Starting reasoning level for that model |
| `imageDelegates` | `provider/model` → `{ provider, model }` | The model that reads images on this one's behalf |
| `imageCapable` | `provider/model` → `true` | Pins image capability when it cannot be discovered |

Effort ids must match the adapter's own level ids; the card lists them, so pick from
there rather than guessing.

dsh-model-advanced README · Startup self-check：Every boot, after the composition settles, the plugin appends one line to
`~/.dsh/health.log` — the one place a silent degradation becomes visible:

```
2026-11-01T02:00:42Z dsh-model-advanced ok   patch=live tool=live defaults=2/2
2026-11-01T02:00:42Z dsh-model-advanced warn patch=live tool=live defaults=1/2 stale=deepseek/old-model
```

dsh-model-advanced README · Startup self-check：- `patch` — the two prototype decorations are still the functions this plugin
  installed. `dead` means a Harness internal moved and the defaults stop applying.
- `tool` — `inspect_image` registered.
- `defaults` — how many configured defaults were read back from
  `resolveModelInfo` and found to name a level their model still offers. `stale=`
  names the ones that do not, which is what a renamed effort id looks like.

Read it with:

dsh-model-advanced README · Startup self-check：```sh
tail -n 2 ~/.dsh/health.log        # both plugins, when both are installed
grep -v ' ok ' ~/.dsh/health.log   # only problems
```

Set `DSH_HEALTH_LOG` to write somewhere else. A diagnostics failure never stops the
plugin from loading.

dsh-model-advanced README · The warning you see in the app：A failed check is also raised in the client: the composer shows a warning toast — the
same primitive the app's own notices use — saying how many defaults are not applying.
It appears once per page load, retires on its own, and renders nothing at all when the
plugin is healthy.
section: The warning you see in the app

text:
dsh-model-advanced README · The warning you see in the app：The client decides this from the model catalogue rather than from a log: the host half
reports the configured level as `reasoning.defaultEffort`, so a default that is
configured but *not* reported means the decoration is gone. A model that is no longer
in your configuration is ignored — that is stale configuration, not a broken seam.
section: The warning you see in the app

text:
dsh-model-advanced README · The warning you see in the app：To see the warning deliberately, set a default to a reasoning level its model does not
offer (the card lists only valid levels, so edit the settings document directly) and
restart. Remove the entry and restart again to clear it.

Verified on a real boot of DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.5 (macOS desktop profile) on
2026-11-01, with five configured model defaults:

```
2026-11-01T02:03:32Z dsh-model-advanced ok   patch=live tool=live defaults=5/5
```
section: The warning you see in the app

text:
dsh-model-advanced README · The warning you see in the app：That line is the compatibility datapoint worth checking after you upgrade: it names the
Harness version this plugin was last confirmed against.
section: The warning you see in the app

text:
dsh-model-advanced README · Compatibility：This plugin reaches into Harness internals rather than wrapping a public extension
point, which is a deliberate trade: there is no public seam for "change this model's
default effort" or "read this image for a model that cannot".

What that means in practice:

dsh-model-advanced README · Compatibility：- **It fails soft, and silently.** Every decoration and hook is wrapped so that a
  failure leaves the turn exactly as it would have been. If a future Harness release
  renames `resolveModelInfo` or `resolveCallConfig`, the card still renders and saves
  settings, but the defaults stop being applied — with no error in the UI. The startup
  self-check is the detector: look for `patch=dead` in `~/.dsh/health.log` first.
- **It is version-coupled.** Tested against the Harness build it was developed on.
- **No automated tests.** The behaviour depends on a live composition (LLM runtime,
  settings documents, agent sessions) that is not practical to fake convincingly; the
  seams above are the thing to verify by hand after an upgrade.

dsh-model-advanced README · Known limits：- **DeepSeek's adapters register no model discovery**, so their models report image
  capability only through provider configuration (API-key routes) or the adapter's own
  catalogue (account route, when the app has it). For a model whose capability is
  genuinely unknown, use the pin checkbox.
- **The composer's Effort menu lists the adapter's level names.** The card uses the
  same names deliberately, so the two never disagree.
- **Defaults changed while the app runs** align the global default selection at the
  next start (or after re-picking the model).
- **Multi-model routes** take reasoning-level names from each model, but the stored
  default is always per model.
- **A delegate call is a real model call** — it costs tokens. It is made once per
  image per session, plus once per `inspect_image` call.

dsh-model-advanced README · Layout：| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | Host half: config schema, prototype decorations, handoff, `inspect_image` |
| `lib/client.js` | Browser half: the card in the Models page footer slot |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch that inserts the plugin row |
| `docs/advanced-model-settings.png` | Screenshot of the card, shown at the top |
dsh-model-advanced README · License：MIT.

provider independent, and what lets a model the adapters cannot describe still get a

section: How the default reasoning level is applied

text:
dsh-model-advanced README · How the default reasoning level is applied：1. **`resolveModelInfo`** is decorated so the model catalogue *states* the configured
   level, and so the composer's Effort menu opens on it.
2. **`resolveCallConfig`** is decorated so selecting a model *without* naming a level
   saves the configured level instead of the adapter's own default.
3. An **`agent/request` waterfall** covers entry points that never pick a level at all.
4. A **startup reconciliation** (once, after the composition transaction settles)
   aligns the global default selection with the configured level.

text:
dsh-model-advanced README · How image handoff works：Configure a delegate for a model that does not read images. Then, when a turn carries
an image:

dsh-model-advanced README · How image handoff works：1. The delegate is called **once**, with a layout-preserving transcription
   instruction: a one-line summary, reading order, every text region with its
   approximate bounding box on a 0–1000 scale, tables as GFM, and notes for diagrams
   and UI state.
2. The result is appended to the step as an image transcript note naming the image id.
3. That note carries a `[dsh-image-handoff:<id>]` marker which is read back from
   session history, so retries and later turns **never re-bill the delegate**.
4. The image itself stays in the conversation; the wire to the text-only model still
   carries a placeholder, never the image. The transcript is what the model reads.

dsh-model-advanced README · How image handoff works：For follow-up questions the model calls:

```text
inspect_image(image_id, question)
```

which hands the same image to the delegate again with the question. This exists so a
text-only model is not stuck with a single fixed reading of an image forever.

A delegate failure does not end the turn — it becomes a note in the transcript saying
what could not be read.

dsh-model-advanced README · Discovering which models read images：Capability is resolved in this order, cheapest first:

1. **The provider's own configuration** — the model's declared input modalities in
   its settings namespace.
2. **`discoverModels`**, asked only for models the configuration does not describe, so
   an ordinary page load stays offline.
3. **Inference from the same model id** served by another configured route.
4. **A checkbox** — *"This model reads images"* — when all of the above are unknown,
   which pins the answer for that model.

dsh-model-advanced README · Configure by hand：The card writes this namespace; it can also be edited directly.

```yaml
- id: model-advanced
  config:
    modelDefaults:
      "deepseek/deepseek-chat": high

dsh-model-advanced README · Configure by hand：| Key | Shape | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `modelDefaults` | `provider/model` → effort id | Starting reasoning level for that model |
| `imageDelegates` | `provider/model` → `{ provider, model }` | The model that reads images on this one's behalf |
| `imageCapable` | `provider/model` → `true` | Pins image capability when it cannot be discovered |

Effort ids must match the adapter's own level ids; the card lists them, so pick from
there rather than guessing.

dsh-model-advanced README · Startup self-check：Every boot, after the composition settles, the plugin appends one line to
`~/.dsh/health.log` — the one place a silent degradation becomes visible:

```
2026-11-01T02:00:42Z dsh-model-advanced ok   patch=live tool=live defaults=2/2
2026-11-01T02:00:42Z dsh-model-advanced warn patch=live tool=live defaults=1/2 stale=deepseek/old-model
```

dsh-model-advanced README · Startup self-check：- `patch` — the two prototype decorations are still the functions this plugin
  installed. `dead` means a Harness internal moved and the defaults stop applying.
- `tool` — `inspect_image` registered.
- `defaults` — how many configured defaults were read back from
  `resolveModelInfo` and found to name a level their model still offers. `stale=`
  names the ones that do not, which is what a renamed effort id looks like.

Read it with:

dsh-model-advanced README · Startup self-check：```sh
tail -n 2 ~/.dsh/health.log        # both plugins, when both are installed
grep -v ' ok ' ~/.dsh/health.log   # only problems
```

Set `DSH_HEALTH_LOG` to write somewhere else. A diagnostics failure never stops the
plugin from loading.

dsh-model-advanced README · The warning you see in the app：A failed check is also raised in the client: the composer shows a warning toast — the
same primitive the app's own notices use — saying how many defaults are not applying.
It appears once per page load, retires on its own, and renders nothing at all when the
plugin is healthy.
section: The warning you see in the app

text:
dsh-model-advanced README · The warning you see in the app：The client decides this from the model catalogue rather than from a log: the host half
reports the configured level as `reasoning.defaultEffort`, so a default that is
configured but *not* reported means the decoration is gone. A model that is no longer
in your configuration is ignored — that is stale configuration, not a broken seam.

offer (the card lists only valid levels, so edit the settings document directly) and
restart. Remove the entry and restart again to clear it.

text:
dsh-model-advanced README · Compatibility：This plugin reaches into Harness internals rather than wrapping a public extension
point, which is a deliberate trade: there is no public seam for "change this model's
default effort" or "read this image for a model that cannot".

What that means in practice:

dsh-model-advanced README · Compatibility：- **It fails soft, and silently.** Every decoration and hook is wrapped so that a
  failure leaves the turn exactly as it would have been. If a future Harness release
  renames `resolveModelInfo` or `resolveCallConfig`, the card still renders and saves
  settings, but the defaults stop being applied — with no error in the UI. The startup
  self-check is the detector: look for `patch=dead` in `~/.dsh/health.log` first.
- **It is version-coupled.** Tested against the Harness build it was developed on.
- **No automated tests.** The behaviour depends on a live composition (LLM runtime,
  settings documents, agent sessions) that is not practical to fake convincingly; the
  seams above are the thing to verify by hand after an upgrade.

dsh-model-advanced README · Known limits：- **DeepSeek's adapters register no model discovery**, so their models report image
  capability only through provider configuration (API-key routes) or the adapter's own
  catalogue (account route, when the app has it). For a model whose capability is
  genuinely unknown, use the pin checkbox.
- **The composer's Effort menu lists the adapter's level names.** The card uses the
  same names deliberately, so the two never disagree.
- **Defaults changed while the app runs** align the global default selection at the
  next start (or after re-picking the model).
- **Multi-model routes** take reasoning-level names from each model, but the stored
  default is always per model.
- **A delegate call is a real model call** — it costs tokens. It is made once per
  image per session, plus once per `inspect_image` call.

dsh-model-advanced README · dsh-model-advanced：Per-model default reasoning level and image handoff for text-only models — added to
the existing **Settings → Models** page.

Model adapters describe a model once, provider-wide and statically. Two things an
agent actually needs cannot be expressed that way:

dsh-model-advanced README · dsh-model-advanced：- **The level a conversation should start at, per model.** A fast model and a
  reasoning model on the same provider usually want different defaults, but an adapter
  exposes a single provider-wide effort.
- **What happens when a text-only model is handed an image.** Today the image is
  dropped or the turn fails. It should be read by a model that *can* see, and the
  reading should stay in the conversation.

dsh-model-advanced README · dsh-model-advanced：This plugin adds a card at the bottom of the Models page that configures both, and
implements the runtime behaviour behind them.

*The card this plugin adds, at the bottom of **Settings → Models**: a starting reasoning
level for each model, and — for a model that cannot see — the model that reads images on
its behalf.*

dsh-model-advanced README · Install：Requires a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) install
with the plugin manager.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:drm-nz/dsh-model-advanced
```

Then **restart the app**. This plugin has a host half (`lib/index.js`) and a browser
half (`lib/client.js`); the host half loads at boot, and the browser half is served
from the installed package, so neither picks up without a restart.

dsh-model-advanced README · From a local checkout：```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-model-advanced
```

or add the `link:` dependency to the profile's `package.json`, run `pnpm install` there,
and restart. A linked package resolves its dependencies and peers from its own
directory, so they must be installed there too.

dsh-model-advanced README · From a local checkout：The shipped `cordis.patch.yml` names its entry **bare** (`dsh-model-advanced`), not
relatively. A `link:` install's real directory sits outside `node_modules`, and this
plugin imports Harness packages, so a bare name resolves through the profile's
dependency mapping — a relative name would bypass it and the import would fail.

To remove it:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-model-advanced
```

dsh-model-advanced README · From a local checkout：Requires the Harness packages it builds on (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`,
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`) to resolve from the profile, and
they should match the running Harness version — the plugin decorates runtime
prototypes, so it is version-coupled by nature. See *Compatibility* below.
